subject: reasoning
question:
In a certain code language,

'A + B' means 'A is the mother of B',

'A - B' means 'A is the daughter of B',

'A × B' means 'A is the son of B' and

'A ÷ B' means 'A is the brother of B'.

How is F related to C if 'C - D ÷ E × F + G'?
solution:

Given Expression: ‘C - D ÷ E × F + G’

C is the daughter of D, D is the brother of E, E is the son of F, F is the Mother of G.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bff6a06bc42d7890a52590a7edc278aee9b5b0e47cfc81e043547a1426ab1112.png] [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af5222da878e0aef4d1832b38dd50392fc5ff6968df1dce8d2f72bcf43fd8177.png] 

So, F is Father’s mother of C.

Hence, the correct answer is *'Option 2'.*
